# Reference Notes 

Made By Abhik Biswas 

Here is the step-by-step algebraic breakdown of **HOW** we arrive at ∆ _E_ = _mlµBB_ . 

## **Step 1: Magnetic Potential Energy Equation** 

The potential energy _U_ of any magnetic dipole _⃗µL_ in an external magnetic field _⃗B_ is given by the classic formula: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
U =  −⃗µL ·⃗B<br><!-- End of picture text -->

If we align the external magnetic field along the _z_ -axis, so _⃗B_ = (0 _,_ 0 _, B_ ), the dot product simplifies to just the _z_ -components: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
U =  −µL,zB — (Equation 1)<br><!-- End of picture text -->

## **Step 2: Relating Magnetic Moment (** _µL,z_ **) to Angular Momentum (** _Lz_ **)** 

First, why is an orbiting electron a magnet? An electron of mass _me_ and charge _−e_ moving in a circle has: 

- Orbital Angular Momentum: _L_ = _mevr_ 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
• Current created by the loop: I = T e = 2 evπr<br>• Area of the loop: A  =  πr 2<br><!-- End of picture text -->

The magnetic moment magnitude is: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
µL =  I × A  = ( 2 evπr ) ( πr 2 ) = evr 2<br><!-- End of picture text -->

Substituting _vr_ = _mLe_<sup>intothisgives:</sup> 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
µL = L<br>( 2 me e )<br><!-- End of picture text -->

Because the electron has a **negative charge** ( _−e_ ), the magnetic moment vector _⃗µL_ points in the **exact opposite direction** to the angular momentum vector _⃗L_ : 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
µL =  − L<br>( 2 me e )<br><!-- End of picture text -->

Notes 

2 

Looking only at the _z_ -component: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
µL,z =  − Lz — (Equation 2)<br>( 2 me e )<br><!-- End of picture text -->

## **Step 3: Substitute Equation 2 into Equation 1** 

Now, plug _µL,z_ into the potential energy formula from Step 1: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
U =  −µL,zB<br>U =  − − Lz B<br>[ ( 2 me e ) ]<br><!-- End of picture text -->

Notice that the **two minus signs cancel each other out** : 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
U = LzB — (Equation 3)<br>( 2 me e )<br><!-- End of picture text -->

## **Step 4: Apply Quantum Mechanics (Quantization of** _Lz_ **)** 

In quantum mechanics, the _z_ -component of orbital angular momentum _Lz_ cannot take any continuous value. It is restricted (quantized) to discrete values: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
Lz =  mlh ¯ where ml ∈{−l, −l  + 1 , . . . ,  + l}<br><!-- End of picture text -->

Substitute _Lz_ = _mlh_ ¯ into Equation 3: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
U = ( mlh ¯) B<br>( 2 me e )<br><!-- End of picture text -->

Rearrange the terms by grouping the constants together: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
U =  ml B — (Equation 4)<br>( 2 emh ¯ e )<br><!-- End of picture text -->

## **Step 5: Define the Bohr Magneton (** _µB_ **)** 

To keep equations clean, physicists define all those physical constants inside the parentheses as a single constant called the **Bohr Magneton (** _µB_ **)** : 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
µB ≡ eh ¯<br>2 me<br><!-- End of picture text -->

Replacing ( 2 _<u>emh</u>_ ¯ _e_ ) with _µB_ in Equation 4 gives the final energy shift (∆ _E_ ): 

**￿E** = **ml** _µ_ **BB**
